utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I will ask the Registrar to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-05-88-A, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I have the appearances, beginning with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. On behalf of the Prosecution, Peter Kremer. I'm assisted by Ingrid Elliott and Francois Boudreault, and our Case Manager with us today is Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kremer. And for the Defence, can we begin with counsel for Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. On behalf of Mr. Vujadin Popovic, Zoran Zivanovic, lead counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then for Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon. My name is John Ostojic. I'm here for Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Jelena Nikolic, counsel for Mr. Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Miletic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning [as interpreted]. I represent Mr. Milanovic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DAVIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Simon Davis, co-counsel to Peter Haynes. I'm accompanied today by Kinga Tibori.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Today we have Mr. Borovcanin. Mr. Borovcanin has not appealed, but I have exceptionally allowed him to be present so that when the time comes, he will be able to make any representation that he wishes about the conditions of his detention or, indeed, about any other matter relating to the case.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction: Mrs. Fauveau represented Mr. Miletic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Good afternoon. Tatjana Cmeric on behalf of Mr. Borovcanin, and I thank you for having us here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to deal with some matters -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting, Your Honour. My name is David Josse. I'm here with Miroslav Kusic, our Case Manager, for the absent Milan Gvero. We made inquiries of the Chamber and were told that we did need to attend this particular hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, you are very welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I was indicating that before I hear from the appellants, whether they have anything to say, I have some matters that I wish to deal with. On the 8th of September last year, the notice of appeal for Mr. Popovic, Mr. Beara, Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Miletic, Mr. Pandurevic, and the Prosecution were filed. The notices of appeal for Mr. Beara, Mr. Miletic, and the Prosecution were filed publicly. I note, however, that at present only the confidential versions of the notices of appeal for Mr. Popovic, Mr. Nikolic, and Mr. Pandurevic have been filed. I am, therefore, ordering that the public redacted versions of these appellants' notices of appeal be filed no later than the 9th of March, 2011. On the 20th of October, 2010, I issued a decision granting, in part, several motions for extension of time and word limits, and ordering that: The appellant briefs be filed no later than the 21st of January, 2011; that the respondents' briefs be filed no later than the 4th of April, 2011; and that the reply briefs be filed no later than the 2nd of May, 2011. I further ordered that: The appeal briefs for Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Popovic, Mr. Beara, and Mr. Miletic not exceed 40.000 words each; that the Prosecution's response brief not exceed 190.000 words; and that the reply briefs of Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Popovic, Mr. Beara, and Mr. Miletic not exceed 12.000 words each. On the 21st of January, 2011, the appeal briefs for Mr. Popovic, Mr. Beara, Mr. Miletic, Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Pandurevic, and the Prosecution were filed, and I note that today Mr. Nikolic filed a confidential corrigendum to his appellant's brief, clarifying typographical errors. The Prosecution filed the confidential version of its appeal brief on the 21st of January and the public redacted version of its brief on the 25th of January, 2011, but I note that to date only the confidential versions of the appeal briefs for the remaining appellants have been provided. As such, I now order that the public redacted versions of these appeal briefs be filed no later than the 11th of April, 2011. As far as the parties' books of authorities are concerned, I see that the Prosecution and counsel for Mr. Nikolic and Mr. Pandurevic each filed their book of authorities on the 21st of January, 2011. I also note that the Miletic Defence filed its book of authorities on the 24th of January, 2011, and that an addendum to Mr. Nikolic's book of authorities was filed on the 27th of January, 2011. We are still awaiting Mr. Popovic's and Mr. Beara's book of authorities, and consequently, I now order counsel for those appellants to file their client's book of authorities no later than the 23rd of February, 2011. I now want to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I now wish to inquire into the conditions of detention and the state of the health of each of the appellants present, and I'm going to begin with Mr. Popovic. Please stand. May I ask, Mr. Popovic, whether you wish to raise any concerns regarding your health or conditions of your detention. THE APPELLANT POPOVIC: [Interpretation] As far as detention or my health are concerned, there's nothing I would raise at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated. We'll now turn to Mr. Beara, and may I ask you the same question, Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to ask you the same question, Mr. Beara, and that is whether you wish to raise any concerns regarding your health or the conditions of your detention. THE APPELLANT BEARA: [Interpretation] Nothing in particular, Your Honour. Everything is as it should be and as is usual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I am very pleased to hear that. THE APPELLANT BEARA: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And Mr. Nikolic, do you have any matters to raise regarding your detention or your health? THE APPELLANT NIKOLIC: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm in good health, and I don't have any specific issues to raise regarding detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Miletic. THE APPELLANT MILETIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as regards detention or my health, well, it's as normal for my age, so I don't have anything in particular to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And Mr. Pandurevic. THE APPELLANT PANDUREVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, detention, the conditions are all right, and my health is satisfactory. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Borovcanin. THE APPELLANT BOROVCANIN: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I don't have anything in particular to raise, save for the fact that in the meantime, I met with the Registrar or his representative on three occasions regarding my status. And apart from that, there's nothing specific I'd like to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We appear to be in a state of perfection. May I ask whether counsel would wish to raise any matter? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Not at the moment, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The only issue that comes up is the translation of the trial judgement. My client has mentioned, on several occasions, that I should inquire. We just don't know when we'll be able to get that in the language that they could understand so that they could assist us at least part of the appeal. So it's important. Although we've translated most of it or some of it directly related to him, I think it's important, based on the Rules, that he be given a complete translation in a language which he understands. And that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, you're absolutely right, he's entitled to have it translated. I'm going to make an inquiry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, as you know, it's a very long judgement, running into some 800 pages. The translators are working as fast as they can, and the information that I have is that the translation should be completed before the Christmas recess of this year. Now, that does appear to be a little way off, and I will follow up on it and contact you with the latest information. Does any other counsel have any matter to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. DAVIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of Mr. Pandurevic, I put my learned friend Mr. Kremer on notice earlier, before the hearing, and I'll give, obviously, notice to Your Honour and the Court that hopefully on Friday of this week, an urgent motion for provisional release is to be submitted on behalf of Mr. Pandurevic. I'm not going to go into the basis of that or the motion, itself, for today's purposes, but for obvious reasons he would wish that that be dealt with urgently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that is the custom. A motion for provisional release affecting the liberty of the person is always dealt with speedily. Any matters from the Prosecution or any other counsel? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could I invite the court go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There being no other matters to be raised, the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: at 3.23 p.m.
